    Project Budget Calculator

    USD amounts use only prices you enter. Blank prices are unquoted, not free. No labor estimate is included. Add taxes, delivery or other costs yourself.

    Methodology and assumptions

    Gross wall area = 2 × (length + width) × height. Deduct count × width × height for doors and windows. Ceiling area = length × width, calculated separately. Coating quantity = net area × coats ÷ label coverage × (1 + allowance ÷ 100). Primer uses its own coverage and coats. Metric values convert through 1 ft = 0.3048 m and 1 US gallon = 3.785411784 L.

    The existing-area option uses an already net paintable area; it does not deduct openings again. Separate paints are rounded independently to the chosen container size. Budget = selected, unowned purchase quantities × your unit prices + additional costs, then contingency. Missing quotes mean an incomplete budget. Material prices and labor are never fetched.

    How Paint Calculation Works

    Paint quantity depends on the surface area, the product's coverage rate, and the number of coats. A small extra allowance helps account for texture, application method and touch-ups.

    Key Factors

    • Surface type and texture
    • Paint type and finish
    • Manufacturer coverage rate
    • Number of coats
    • Application method
    • Color change and primer

    For accurate results, measure each surface and deduct openings you will not paint. Use the coverage on your product label, allow for texture and extra coats, and keep paint from the same batch for touch-ups.

    Frequently Asked Questions

    How many square feet does a gallon of paint cover?

    Many paints specify a coverage range around 300–400 square feet per gallon for a single coat, but check your exact product label.

    Should I plan for two coats?

    Two coats are common for an even finish. The ideal number depends on the old and new colors, paint type and surface.

    How much extra paint should I buy?

    An allowance around 10–15% can be a useful planning starting point, depending on surface and application.
